Logan]] (2018–2020) | highlights = * [[NABC Player of the Year#Junior College Player of the Year|NABC NJCAA Player of the Year]] (2020) * 2× First-team [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] DI All-American (2019, 2020) * [[Great Rivers Athletic Conference|GRAC]] Player of the Year (2020) * GRAC Freshman of the Year (2019) * 2× All-GRAC Team (2019, 2020) | medal_templates = }} '''Jayden Scrubb''' (born September 1, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[John A. Logan College|John A. Logan Volunteers]] and was named [[NABC Player of the Year#Junior College Player of the Year|NABC NJCAA Division I Player of the Year]] as a sophomore. Scrubb was originally committed to continue his college career with [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] but instead declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Scrubb grew up on the west end of [[Louisville, Kentucky]]. He grew up rooting for his hometown team, the [[Louisville Cardinals]]. His father described his hometown as "a tougher part of town, which some would consider [[Underclass|the hood]]."{{cite web |last1=Petzold |first1=Evan |title='Never give up': Jayden Scrubb's journey from school struggles to Team USA hopeful |url=https://gazette.com/sports/never-give-up-jayden-scrubb-s-journey-from-school-struggles/article_911100ae-9105-11e9-957d-0bbd005b74eb.html |website=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]] |accessdate=September 25, 2019 |date=June 17, 2019}} Scrubb's family dynamics negatively affected his academics.{{cite web |last1=Frakes |first1=Jason |title=Trinity's Scrubb had to find his way in classroom before prospering on basketball court |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/02/16/trinitys-scrubb-had-find-his-way-classroom-before-prospering-basketball-court/333763002/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=September 24, 2019 |date=February 16, 2018}} ==High school career== As a freshman, Scrubb attended [[Central High School (Louisville, Kentucky)|Central High School]] in Louisville but was not allowed on the basketball team due to poor academic performance. He sometimes took medications because he believed he had a [[learning disability]]. In the summer after failing his freshman year, Scrubb studied to meet the minimum requirements to start his sophomore year. As a sophomore, he transferred from Central to the more esteemed [[Trinity High School (Louisville)|Trinity High School]], a [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] in Louisville, on a need-based [[School voucher|voucher]].{{cite web |last1=Greer |first1=Jeff |title=How Jayden Scrubb emerged as maybe the top juco prospect in the country |url=https://theathletic.com/1050466/2019/07/11/how-jayden-scrubb-emerged-as-maybe-the-top-juco-prospect-in-the-country/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=September 25, 2019 |date=July 11, 2019}} In his first basketball season at Trinity, Scrubb occasionally practiced with the [[varsity team]] but never played in games because his coach found his work ethic lacking. In his junior year, he enrolled in an alternative academic program at Trinity through which he joined smaller classes and made progress in school. Over the summer, he also claimed to grow from {{height|ft=6|in=2}} to {{height|ft=6|in=6}}. In his junior season, Scrubb averaged 16 points per game and was named Seventh Region Player of the Year by ''[[The Courier-Journal]]''.{{cite web |last1=Frakes |first1=Jason |title=Trinity's Scrubb tops All-Seventh Region team |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2017/02/24/trinitys-scrubb-tops-all-seventh-region-team/98355840/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=September 24, 2019 |date=February 24, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Drew |title=Trinity wing Jay Scrubb aims for top college basketball programs |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky-high-school-sports/2017/07/22/trinity-wing-jay-scrubb-aims-top-college-basketball-programs/501918001/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=September 24, 2019 |date=July 22, 2017}} As a senior, he averaged 17.8 points and 7.1 rebounds per game. Scrubb repeated as Seventh Region Player of the Year and was a finalist for the [[Kentucky Mr. Basketball]] award.{{cite web |last1=Frakes |first1=Jason |title=Trinity High School star Jay Scrubb signs to play basketball at Illinois junior college |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/04/11/trinity-high-school-jay-scrubb-signs-illinois-junior-college/509648002/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=September 22, 2019 |date=April 11, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Frakes |first1=Jason |title=Check out Courier Journal's All-Sixth Region, All-Seventh Region basketball teams |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/02/22/courier-journals-all-sixth-region-all-seventh-region-basketball-teams-announced/360558002/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=September 22, 2019 |date=February 22, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Frakes |first1=Jason |title=Kentucky's Mr. and Miss Basketball awards: Meet the finalists |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/02/16/finalists-announced-kentuckys-mr-and-miss-basketball-awards/342516002/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=September 24, 2019 |date=February 16, 2018}} ==College career== On April 11, 2018, Scrubb signed to play [[college basketball]] for [[John A. Logan College]], a [[junior college]] in [[Carterville, Illinois]]. He joined a junior college team because he was academically ineligible for an [[NCAA Division I]] scholarship, although he had intentions of later transferring to a Division I program. Scrubb made his college debut on November 1, 2018, scoring 12 points in a 106–81 win over [[Motlow State Community College|Motlow State]].{{cite web |title=John A. Logan routs Motlow in impressive season opener |url=http://www.wsiltv.com/story/39404873/john-a-logan-routs-motlow-in-impressive-season-opener |publisher=[[WSIL-TV]] |accessdate=September 26, 2019 |date=November 2, 2018}} On December 8, he scored 25 points and a season-high 20 rebounds in a 99–69 victory over [[Southeastern Illinois College]].{{cite web |title=Scrubb leads Logan to win over SIC |url=https://thesouthern.com/sports/college/basketball/scrubb-leads-logan-to-win-over-sic/article_095f885e-df0b-506e-8bc3-eb0abe8d7f01.html |website=[[The Southern Illinoisan]] |accessdate=September 26, 2019 |date=December 8, 2018}} Scrubb, on January 16, posted a season-best 40 points and 13 rebounds in a 105–93 win over [[Rend Lake College]].{{cite web |last1=Walker |first1=Justin |title=Volunteers overcome adversity, beat Rend Lake |url=http://www.dailyregister.com/sports/20190117/volunteers-overcome-adversity-beat-rend-lake |website=[[The Daily Register]] |accessdate=September 27, 2019 |date=January 17, 2019}} He finished the season averaging 20.2 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 1.6 blocks per game, shooting 46 percent from three-point range.{{cite web |title=Jay Scrubb |url=https://www.loganvols.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/bios/scrubb_jay_oxov?view=career&pos=sh |publisher=John A. Logan College Athletics |accessdate=September 27, 2019}} Scrubb was named [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] (NJCAA) Region 24 Player of the Year and [[Great Rivers Athletic Conference]] (GRAC) Freshman of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Weiler |first1=Mark |title=Men's Junior College Basketball / All-GRAC and All-Region 24 Teams |url=https://www.freedom929.com/2019/03/14/mens-junior-college-basketball-all-grac-and-all-region-24-teams/ |publisher=[[WSEI (FM)]] |accessdate=September 27, 2019 |date=March 14, 2019}} He also earned first-team NJCAA Division I All-American honors.{{cite web |title=Logan's Scrubb, Sloan named All-American |url=https://thesouthern.com/sports/sports-logan-s-scrubb-sloan-named-all-american/article_6c3f07d0-39a6-5836-aff3-ab992d274ac3.html |website=[[The Southern Illinoisan]] |accessdate=September 27, 2019 |date=April 10, 2019}} Scrubb parlayed his freshman success at John A. Logan into offers from many NCAA Division I programs, including [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web |last1=Marcum |first1=Jason |title=Jay Scrubb includes Kentucky in top 10 |url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2019/9/1/20843617/uk-basketball-jay-scrubb-louisville-cardinals-recruiting-alabama-recruit |publisher=A Sea of Blue |accessdate=September 27, 2019 |date=September 1, 2019}} He was ranked as the number one junior college recruit in his class after his first season.{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Jay Scrubb planning out visits |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Jay-Scrubb-JUCO-No-1-Player-135742183/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=September 27, 2019 |date=September 17, 2019}} On September 28, 2019, Scrubb committed to play for Louisville following an additional year at John A. Logan.{{cite web |last1=Rutherford |first1=Mike |title=Top-ranked JuCo player Jay Scrubb commits to Louisville |url=https://www.cardchronicle.com/2019/9/28/20888830/top-ranked-juco-player-jay-scrubb-commits-to-louisville |publisher=Card Chronicle |accessdate=September 28, 2019 |date=September 28, 2019}} On November 1, 2019, in his sophomore season opener, Scrubb scored 13 points and battled foul trouble in an upset loss to [[Otero Junior College]].{{cite web |last1=Hefferman |first1=Todd |title=Unranked Otero beats fourth-ranked Logan in season opener |url=https://thesouthern.com/sports/college/salukimania/unranked-otero-beats-fourth-ranked-logan-in-season-opener/article_6c75f2f2-1083-536c-8811-946e4fd06a88.html |website=[[The Southern Illinoisan]] |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=November 2, 2019}} On December 6, it was announced that he had been suspended indefinitely after returning to campus late after [[Thanksgiving]] break.{{cite web |title=Logan's Scrubb suspended indefinitely |url=https://thesouthern.com/sports/college/basketball/logan-s-scrubb-suspended-indefinitely/article_576b1d95-187d-5ed5-b4ed-9fe6b4410af5.html |website=[[The Southern Illinoisan]] |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=December 6, 2019}} As a sophomore, Scrubb averaged 21.9 points, 6.8 rebounds and 2.7 assists a game.{{cite news |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Louisville commit Jay Scrubb declares for the NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Jay-Scrubb-Louisville-NBA-Draft-145374361/ |accessdate=March 29, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 25, 2020}} After the season, he was named the [[NABC Player of the Year#Junior College Player of the Year|NABC NJCAA Division I Player of the Year]] and repeated as a first-team NJCAA Division I All-American, while being named GRAC Player of the Year.{{cite news |last1= |first1=|title= NABC Announces NJCAA Award Winners |url= https://www.nabc.com/nabc_releases/2020/njcaa_awards |accessdate= April 8, 2020 |work=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] |date=April 8, 2020}} On March 25, 2020, Scrubb declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] while maintaining his eligibility and did not immediately sign with an agent. On April 9, he announced that he would sign with an agent and forgo his remaining college basketball eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=JUCO standout and Louisville commit Jay Scrubb signs with agent |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Jay-Scrubb-Going-Pro-Louisville-145879416/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=April 9, 2020 |date=April 9, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| 2018–19 | style="text-align:left;"| [[John A.
